tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on symptom/intent-based triggers (connection errors, timeouts, error replies, alarms) rather than implementation details, explicitly lists many trigger contexts including implicit ones ('even if only the symptom is described'), and explicitly scopes out-of-domain cases. It is a dense but bounded paragraph, appropriate given the breadth of triggers it needs to cover.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when an application that uses an Amazon ElastiCache cache (node-based or serverless; Valkey, Redis OSS or Memcached) sees connection errors or timeouts... Use it even if only the symptom is described. Do not use it to create, size or migrate caches, or for self-managed Valkey or Redis (for example on EC2).

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense and domain-specific throughout — it states ElastiCache-specific rules, metric names, and operational constraints without explaining general concepts the agent already knows (e.g., no definitions of what a cache or CloudWatch is).
tests.evidence: G1: use the classic metric where OpenTelemetry has no equivalent. That is CurrItems, CurrVolatileItems, latency percentiles, ReplicationLag...

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed tables (error codes, metric thresholds, mitigation rows) are consistently pushed into references/ files rather than embedded inline, even within conditional branches like Step 3 and Step 6.
tests.evidence: Load [references/error-replies.md](references/error-replies.md) to map it to its cause.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file in references/ is linked with a markdown link somewhere in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is accompanied by a clear trigger condition for when to load it (e.g., deployment discovery before recommending features, error-replies.md when an error reply appears).
tests.evidence: When the operator quotes an engine error reply, or the error metrics show one, load [references/error-replies.md](references/error-replies.md) to map it to its cause.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/ without traversal or absolute paths.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, risky operations (mitigation application, data-plane commands) are given exact, prescriptive steps, while judgment-heavy tasks (judging causes, reporting) are described with rationale and flexibility to adapt per incident.
tests.evidence: Pre-check: run the row's read-only checks and quote the values. Stop and say why if a check fails. ... Mark each cause confirmed ... ruled out ... or unknown

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: When multiple metric paths exist (OpenTelemetry vs classic), the skill gives clear rules for which to use by default and when to fall back to the other, rather than listing them as equal options.
tests.evidence: G1: use the classic metric where OpenTelemetry has no equivalent. ... For node-based Valkey, query both paths.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The workflow teaches a generalizable method for diagnosing any ElastiCache incident (identify deployment, collect evidence, judge causes, validate, report, mitigate) rather than a one-off instance-specific task.
tests.evidence: Name the root cause of an ElastiCache incident from evidence, rule out the lookalike cause that produces the same symptom, and give the operator a fix.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The Rules section (G1-G4) and Scope section explicitly document non-obvious environment-specific pitfalls like missing OTel metrics for Redis OSS, billing gotchas, and dangerous recommendation patterns.
tests.evidence: G4: never recommend a capacity change (a larger node, more shards or replicas, higher serverless limits) for a hot key, an unbounded collection or a client-side cause.

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill does define a structured output format (Step 5: Report with five named parts), satisfying the need for a template for its report-generating purpose.
tests.evidence: Always give all five parts, even when the cause looks obvious. 1. Root cause... 2. Evidence... 3. Ruled out... 4. Remediation... 5. Gaps...

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The Step 5 report template is short (5 bullet items, well under 20 lines) and embedded inline appropriately.
tests.evidence: 1. Root cause: one sentence naming the mechanism, not the symptom. ... 5. Gaps: what could not be verified, with the command that would verify it.
